title: The scan that cuts the line
topic: At Houston Methodist in the Texas Medical Center, a router and an AI tool called Aidoc flag a possible problem on a scan with a heat map and lift that exam to the top of a radiologist's worklist, while the radiologist still reads it and makes the call, and the tool is not perfect.

treatment.logline: At Houston Methodist a router and an AI reorder the line of scans so the urgent one reaches a radiologist first, and the radiologist still makes every call.
treatment.cold_open: A rounded CT scanner with sleepy eyes puffs out a glowing scan card that drops to the bottom of a leaning stack on a radiologist's desk. Before second three the buried card glows orange, waves a tiny flag and starts to rise.
treatment.turn: A false flag. The heat map glows over nothing, the card jumps anyway, and the radiologist frowns and reads it herself. It's not perfect.
treatment.button: The stack again. A new card glows and her hand reaches for it. The machine moves the line. A doctor still reads it.

hero.name: the scan card with a face
hero.why: the exam itself is the thing that waits, worries, glows and climbs, and no film has drawn a scan as a character

scenes.vo: One scan in this long line can't wait. This is Houston Methodist, in the Texas Medical Center.

draw.subject: the grey buried scan card
draw.action: sweats at the bottom of the leaning stack and waves a tiny flag nobody sees
draw.emotion: the radiologist yawns over the top card

draw.subject: the camera
draw.action: pulls back through the window to the Medical Center towers as the stack grows card by card

scenes.vo: A radiologist reads them in order, top to bottom. So how does the urgent one get to the front?

draw.subject: the radiologist
draw.action: pulls the top card off the stack and reads it, tired

draw.subject: the worklist
draw.action: drops away beneath the desk as a long chute of cards with the grey hero card far down

scenes.vo: It starts at the scanner. A router sends the right studies to the AI by itself, and technologists don't touch it. Before, that took setting up each scanner by hand.

draw.subject: the CT scanner with sleepy eyes
draw.action: yawns and puffs the grey hero card out of its ring

visual_events.at_phrase: A router sends the right studies
visual_events.label: Routed automatically

draw.subject: the router
draw.action: flips brass switch tracks and sends cards down the right chutes
draw.emotion: the technologist keeps both hands on the coffee cup, smiling

draw.subject: the technologist
draw.action: climbs from scanner to scanner twisting knobs, sweating

scenes.vo: Then an AI tool called Aidoc reads the images. It flags a possible problem and paints a heat map on the spot it means.

draw.subject: a big scanning lens
draw.action: sweeps across the scan card, slice by slice

draw.subject: a red flag
draw.action: pops up on the card's corner and the card blushes orange for the first time

draw.subject: an orange heat map
draw.action: blooms over one spot on a grey scan slice

scenes.vo: When the concern looks significant, that exam jumps to the top of the radiologist's worklist.

draw.subject: the glowing card
draw.action: rides up the chute while the other cards step aside

draw.subject: the card
draw.action: lands on top of the stack with a bounce

scenes.vo: Some scans can't wait. A pulmonary embolism is a blood clot that breaks loose and travels to the lungs. It can be deadly.

draw.subject: the radiologist
draw.action: widens her eyes at the glowing card

visual_events.at_phrase: a blood clot that breaks loose
visual_events.label: Pulmonary embolism

draw.subject: a red clot
draw.action: breaks off a vein wall and tumbles up the vessel toward the lungs

draw.subject: the lungs
draw.action: flush red as the clot lodges in a branch

scenes.vo: With a stroke, one study estimates a typical patient loses 1.9 million neurons for every minute it goes untreated.

draw.subject: an hourglass of tiny lights
draw.action: flips and starts pouring beside the stack

draw.subject: the counter
draw.action: spins up to 1.9 million as the lights drain

draw.subject: a field of tiny lights
draw.action: goes dark patch by patch while a clock hand sweeps

scenes.vo: So Houston Methodist started with 18 super users testing it, then opened it to roughly 100 radiologists in June.

draw.subject: a wall of dark reading desks
draw.action: slides up into place, its monitors still off

draw.subject: eighteen little radiologist figures
draw.action: pop up in a row of reading desks

draw.subject: the grid of desks
draw.action: multiplies to about a hundred, lights coming on

scenes.vo: Radiologists were skeptical at first. Ginny Torno, who leads the rollout, says even the most skeptical one called it a great tool.

draw.subject: the radiologist
draw.action: crosses her arms and squints at the glowing card

draw.subject: a quote card
draw.action: slides in with her name and title, Sr. Director of IT and Innovation

draw.subject: the radiologist
draw.action: uncrosses her arms and raises a hand in approval

scenes.vo: She also says it isn't perfect, and Aidoc is upfront about that. A flag is a reason to look first, never the answer.

draw.subject: a second, different card
draw.action: glows a heat map over clean healthy tissue and looks sheepish

draw.subject: a quote card
draw.action: slides in reading It's not perfect, but they're upfront about that

draw.subject: a magnifier in the radiologist's hand
draw.action: swings over the flag, which shrinks to a small arrow

scenes.vo: So the radiologist still reads the scan and makes the call. Every time Aidoc gets feedback, it makes a change.

draw.subject: the radiologist
draw.action: opens the card and studies the whole scan herself

draw.subject: a paper note
draw.action: sails back into the scanning lens, which refocuses and turns

scenes.vo: Next, the hospital plans phone alerts for stroke and pulmonary embolism teams, built for triage, not diagnosis. Clinicians would see the images on their phones and call in a response team right away.

draw.subject: a phone in a nurse's hand
draw.action: buzzes and lights with a dotted outline marked next

draw.subject: a triage tag
draw.action: stamps onto the phone screen

draw.subject: the heat-mapped card
draw.action: slides onto the nurse's phone screen

draw.subject: the nurse
draw.action: taps the phone and turns to run, waving the team on

scenes.vo: The machine moves the line. A doctor still reads it.

draw.subject: a new card
draw.action: glows at the bottom of the stack and starts to rise

draw.subject: the radiologist's hand
draw.action: stamps READ on the hero card and reaches for the next
